records.title: Coherent and Incoherent Light Scattering by Single-Atom Wave Packets
records.design: Single-photon scattering from ultracold atomic wave packets
records.summary: The MIT team measured coherent and incoherent light scattering from expanding ultracold atomic wave packets and interpreted the result in terms of atom–photon entanglement and which-path information.
records.limitations: The experiment controls a physical interaction between light and atoms. Directed human attention was outside its design.

records.title: Tunable Einstein-Bohr Recoiling-Slit Gedankenexperiment at the Quantum Limit
records.summary: The USTC team varied the momentum uncertainty of a trapped atom and measured changes in single-photon interference visibility.
records.limitations: The experiment distinguishes effects of momentum transfer from heating in this apparatus. It addresses physical path marking.

records.title: 5-HT2A receptors in layer 5 pyramidal neurons mediate the neuroplastic but not the hallucinogenic effects of psilocybin
records.summary: In genetically modified mice, manipulating 5-HT₂A receptors in layer 5 pyramidal neurons separated psilocybin-induced structural synaptic plasticity from the head-twitch response.
records.limitations: The head-twitch response is a rodent behavioural proxy. The experiment leaves human subjective effects, clinical benefit and microdosing outcomes open.
records.review_state: already covered on the public site

records.title: Microtubule-Stabilizer Epothilone B Delays Anesthetic-Induced Unconsciousness in Rats
records.design: Controlled rat pharmacology with inhaled isoflurane
records.summary: Rats given epothilone B, a microtubule stabiliser, lost their righting reflex later under isoflurane than vehicle-treated rats.
records.limitations: The behavioural endpoint supports investigating microtubules in anaesthesia. A quantum mechanism would require a quantum observable linked to an independently defined biological endpoint.

records.title: The claustrum contributes to working memory maintenance in mice
records.design: Mouse working-memory tasks with neural recording and perturbation
records.summary: Claustrum activity retained information about cues across a delay. Suppressing activity impaired performance on sensory working-memory tasks.
records.limitations: The experiments support a contribution of this circuit to working memory in mice. The separate question of how autobiographical memories persist remains open.
